findings.title: writer activation is still weaker than the original strict-admitted E2 cutover
findings.problem: 171 correctly freezes the legacy window around the original strict-admitted E2 checkpoint, but it only requires B1 writer activation to stop accepting subject-only E2 commits. Under the frozen F1 architecture, Git-only formalIdentityValid checks trailer shape while checkpoint-time Owner temporal admission is completed only by FormalFactReader. Therefore an E2 commit with a syntactically valid subject/trailer set and an owner:<64hex> value that has no matching authorize-checkpoint fact at that boundary can still be exposed by readGitBoundarySummaries and consumed by isPostE2ThreeFileWriterActive. The Proposal does not yet freeze how that consumer is bound to the same strict-admitted cutover.
findings.contractRef: 20260815-169-review-apply F1-RA-001 requiredOutcome/invariant + openspec/changes/archive-and-checkpoint-boundary/design.md Decisions 1-3 + Owner Contract Reset required outcome
findings.invariant: The migration cutover is one authority boundary: the original E2 checkpoint used for bounded legacy compatibility and for post-E2 writer activation must represent the same strict-admitted checkpoint fact. A merely trailer-shaped E2 candidate without checkpoint-time Owner authorization must not activate the writer.
findings.requiredOutcome: Revise the Proposal/Design so post-E2 writer activation is explicitly bound to the same original strict-admitted E2 cutover used by legacy compatibility, not merely to subject/trailer shape. Freeze a feasible implementation/mutation surface that preserves the Git-reader/Owner-authority separation or otherwise proves an equivalent one-authority design, and add the missing negative regression for a full-trailer E2 candidate whose Owner authorization did not exist at the boundary.
acceptance: The Proposal states one shared cutover invariant for legacy admission and writer activation: only the original strict-admitted E2 checkpoint activates the migration writer state.
A migration-lineage E2 commit with exact subject and formal trailers but no matching checkpoint-time authorize-checkpoint Owner fact does not activate the post-E2 writer.
The existing subject-only activation counterexample remains rejected, later duplicate E2 checkpoints cannot move the legacy cutover, and the real e182 strict E2 checkpoint still activates the writer.
Fresh/downstream repositories without the Flowkit internal migration lineage continue to use the current three-file writer by default.

flowkitMutationScope includes every production/test consumer actually required by the chosen design; no Git reader is turned into a second Owner-fact authority merely to avoid widening the proper consumer scope.
